chief_complaint: painful blistering skin rash with peeling of lips, mouth ulcers, and eye inflammation after starting allopurinol
hpi_details: 58M initiated on allopurinol 2 weeks ago presenting with fever, painful dusky purpuric macules, extensive mucosal sloughing in mouth/eyes, and epidermal detachment (<10% BSA).
ideas: He thinks he caught a virulent form of shingles or received a contaminated batch of gout pills that burned his skin from the inside out.
concerns: He is worried that the blistering in his eyes will cause permanent blindness and keep him from driving or working.
expectations: He hopes to receive specialized medicated eye drops to protect his vision, pain relief for his mouth, and a medical leave note for his employer.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management is immediate withdrawal of the culprit drug (here, allopurinol) plus supportive care in a burn unit or ICU setting with urgent ophthalmology involvement, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: painful blistering skin rash with peeling of lips, mouth ulcers, and eye inflammation after starting allopurinol
Key HPI features: 58M initiated on allopurinol 2 weeks ago presenting with fever, painful dusky purpuric macules, extensive mucosal sloughing in mouth/eyes, and epidermal detachment (<10% BSA).
Objective/Exam findings: Febrile; dusky purpuric macules with positive Nikolsky sign, mucosal sloughing of the mouth and conjunctivae, epidermal detachment involving <10% body surface area.
Relevant background/PMH: No significant chronic medical history
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN, if BSA >30%) without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Skin detachment (positive Nikolsky sign).
management_principles: Stop allopurinol immediately — prompt withdrawal of the culprit drug is the single most important intervention
Refer to specialty team and provide comprehensive patient counseling
Assess clinical stability, monitor vital parameters, and perform targeted diagnostic investigations.
Implement targeted therapeutic interventions per evidence-based clinical practice guidelines.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with symptoms of Stevens-Johnson Syndrome SJS TEN: painful blistering skin rash with peeling of lips, mouth ulcers, and eye inflammation after starting allopurinol. 58M initiated on allopurinol 2 weeks ago presenting with fever, painful dusky purpuric macules, extensive mucosal sloughing in mouth/eyes, and epidermal detachment (<10% BSA).
reference_soap.objective: Febrile. Dusky purpuric macules with positive Nikolsky sign, mucosal sloughing of the mouth and conjunctivae, epidermal detachment involving <10% body surface area.
reference_soap.assessment: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) secondary to allopurinol exposure.
reference_soap.plan: 1. Stop allopurinol immediately and document the drug allergy to prevent rechallenge. 2. Transfer to a burn unit or ICU for supportive wound care, fluid/electrolyte management, and infection surveillance. 3. Obtain urgent ophthalmology consultation for ocular mucosal involvement and dermatology/allergy consultation for further management and follow-up.

Select appropriate laboratory and imaging studies for allergy_immunology
Implement evidence-based acute and long-term management strategies

teaching.one_liner: A severe, drug-induced mucocutaneous emergency with skin blistering and detachment plus mouth, eye, or genital mucosal involvement — a medical emergency requiring immediate drug withdrawal.
red_flags: Eye involvement — risk of permanent vision damage
Any mucosal ulceration — mouth, eyes, or genitals

must_ask.say: What new medication did you start, and how many days ago?
Do you have painful sores in your mouth, eyes, or genital area?
Is your skin blistering or peeling off anywhere?

must_ask.objective: Fever and how unwell the patient feels
must_ask.say: Have you had a fever or felt generally very unwell before the rash appeared?
Have you ever had a bad reaction to a medication before?

history.answer: I developed a painful blistering rash all over my body, and my lips are peeling and my mouth is full of sores.
It started three days ago with a burning rash on my chest and face, and it spread quickly across my entire body over the last two days.
The rash is spread all over my chest, back, face, and arms, rather than being confined to just one side or fold.
They look like dark reddish-purple flat spots that developed loose blisters, and now the skin is beginning to peel away.
My skin feels intensely painful and burns like a severe hot-water scald, even when my shirt lightly touches it.
No, the spots stay in place and get worse; they do not fade away or move around within a few hours.
No, I have never had any severe skin rash or blistering like this in my life.
Yes, I started having high fevers and shivering chills two days ago, and I feel completely wiped out.
Yes, my mouth and lips are raw and bleeding, my eyes are red and gritty, and it stings terribly when I urinate.
Yes, the dark purple spots are peeling off in sheets when rubbed, leaving raw, weeping red skin underneath.
My lips and eyelids are very swollen and raw, but my throat is not closing up and I can breathe normally.
My doctor started me on allopurinol two weeks ago because my blood uric acid level was high.
No, I haven't eaten any unfamiliar foods or switched soaps, detergents, cosmetics, or lotions.
No, my wife lives with me and she is completely healthy with no rash or illness.
No, I haven't had any insect or tick bites, and I haven't been hiking or traveling anywhere recently.
No, I have never had asthma, eczema, or chronic allergic allergies.
My muscles and body ache from the high fever, but my joints are not swollen and my nails look completely normal.
I tried applying a gentle moisturizer yesterday, but it stung so intensely that I had to rinse it off immediately.
I have been in a faithful marriage with my wife for thirty years, but I do have painful raw sores on my penis now.
I thought maybe I caught a terrible case of shingles, or that the gout pills I started two weeks ago were tainted and burned me from the inside.
I'm terrified that the blisters spreading into my eyes will permanently blind me so I can never drive or work again.
I do not have any chronic health conditions like diabetes, hypertension, or kidney disease.
I have never had surgery and have never been hospitalized before.
Just the allopurinol 100 milligrams once daily that I started two weeks ago; I take no other pills, painkillers, or herbal supplements.
I have never had an allergic reaction to any medicine before this.
I am a lifelong non-smoker.
I only drink one or two glasses of beer socially on weekends.
I work full-time in an office as an administrator, and I live with my wife.
There is no family history of severe drug eruptions, skin diseases, or autoimmune disorders.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 124/78 mmHg, heart rate is 104 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute, temperature is 38.6 C, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air.
Acutely ill-appearing and distressed male lying cautiously still due to widespread cutaneous pain.
Widespread dusky erythematous and purpuric macules with flaccid blisters, epidermal detachment over roughly 7% of total body surface area, and positive Nikolsky sign upon gentle lateral pressure.
Bilateral severe conjunctival injection, eyelid edema, and mucosal sloughing without gross corneal ulceration.
Severe hemorrhagic crusting of the lips and extensive painful denuded erosions covering the buccal mucosa and palate.
Erythema and painful shallow erosions involving the glans penis and urethral meatus.
Multiple mildly enlarged, mobile, tender anterior cervical lymph nodes bilaterally.
Symmetric chest expansion with skin sloughing across the anterior chest wall, markedly tender to light palpation.
Clear vesicular breath sounds bilaterally without wheezes, crackles, or rhonchi.
Tachycardic regular rhythm with normal first and second heart sounds, without murmurs, gallops, or pericardial friction rubs.
Soft, non-tender abdomen without guarding, rigidity, or rebound tenderness.
